disposition: faithful_port of NodeTest.PubSubWrongTypesTwoSubscribers observable predicates; C++ callback registration and exact scheduling remain outside the claim

private_raw_export.description: Exact staged source tree exported without producer Git metadata into a separate reviewer-owned directory and exclusive CARGO_TARGET_DIR; both source hashes matched and original test source was restored after mutation.
private_raw_export.negative_control: Changing only Node2 subscriber descriptor from gz.msgs.Vector3d to gz.msgs.Int32 delivered the Int32 publication and failed the exact bad=false assertion.

assertion_mapping: Two Node instances share a unique partition; Node1 advertises Int32 on /foo and registers a matching Int32 subscriber, Node2 registers a mismatching Vector3d subscriber.
The Int32(5) value and publisher success are exact.
Connection readiness has its own native 10-second bound; the good receiver begins its fresh 10-second wait only afterward.
Good callback-equivalent receipt decodes Int32 data5, then good=true and bad=false are checked.
Bad subscriber remains live through the good observation and a supplemental 300 ms quiet interval; only exact Timeout is treated as no delivery.
superseded_source: Earlier tree f4df8c642ccdfd59bf2c317ae5826f9a6788ba3f passed a gate but is unapproved: its good 10-second wait began before readiness, and its bad subscriber could drop before good observation. Corrected source dc5763ba fixes both without relaxing the original predicates.
limits: Owned Rust receive threads map observable callbacks; C++ callback registration and precise thread scheduling are not claimed.
Other wrong-type tests and the historical lost-output101 remain separate.
Private replay is correctness evidence only; no timing or throughput conclusion.
